overview: Fabrikam Analytics sells revenue dashboards to B2B sales and RevOps teams. Every name, number and link in this example is fictional.
The homepage states the value clearly and offers two paths (demo and free trial), and the company invests in search: Semrush models a small paid search budget next to a larger organic base.
The weak spots are public reputation and social proof: few reviews, one review site below average, and no customer stories linked from the homepage.

site.diagnosis: Clear headline aimed at the buyer's Monday pipeline review, with demo and trial calls to action above the fold.
site.evidence: Title, description, one H1 and two calls to action read on the homepage; Organization structured data present.
site.opportunity: Add customer logos and one quantified case next to the demo button.
site.risk: Without social proof near the call to action, the trial path carries the whole conversion.

seo.diagnosis: A solid organic base for the company's size: about 1.3k ranking keywords and 214 pages in the sitemap.
seo.opportunity: Comparison and integration pages ("Fabrikam vs", "HubSpot forecast dashboard") are a natural next cluster.

social.diagnosis: LinkedIn is the main channel and is active. Instagram was not identified, which is common and usually fine for this buyer.
social.opportunity: Short product clips from YouTube can be reused on LinkedIn.

paid.diagnosis: The LinkedIn Insight Tag is on the page and Semrush models paid search activity. The Meta Ad Library could not be checked.
paid.opportunity: Retarget trial sign-ups who did not connect a CRM.
paid.risk: Paid search spend is modeled, not measured; confirm with the team before sizing a budget.

content.diagnosis: A blog is linked from the homepage, and LinkedIn posting is estimated at a steady pace.

reputation.diagnosis: Strong on G2 with few reviews; below average on Trustpilot, where about two thirds of complaints were answered.
reputation.opportunity: Ask the 20 happiest accounts for G2 reviews; answer every open Trustpilot complaint.
reputation.risk: Billing complaints are the kind a buyer reads right before a demo.

technical.diagnosis: HTTPS with redirect, mobile viewport, robots.txt and sitemap in place, homepage answered in under 2 seconds.

branding.diagnosis: Consistent identity across the site, LinkedIn and YouTube.

conclusion: Fabrikam has real foundations: a clear offer, a working site, search investment and an active LinkedIn presence.
The two gaps that slow growth are thin public proof and an unanswered complaint trail on one review site.
Start with reputation: answer every open complaint and collect G2 reviews from happy accounts, then add proof next to the demo button.
